canh-ca-nau-qua-doc-kieu-bac.name: Northern Vietnamese fish soup with grilled doc fruit
aliases: Northern fish soup with doc fruit
Vietnamese fish and doc fruit sour soup
canh-ca-nau-qua-doc-kieu-bac.serving_basis: One pot of soup, about four bowls, served with steamed rice.
canh-ca-nau-qua-doc-kieu-bac.description: A Northern Vietnamese fish soup made sour with roasted doc fruit, with tender fish, tomato, dill and scallions. Bếp Việt standardizes the home-size method and adds the strained doc juice gradually so its tartness is easy to adjust.
canh-ca-nau-qua-doc-kieu-bac.finished_dish: Clear, gently sour broth with just-cooked carp, intact tomato wedges and fragrant dill.
canh-ca-nau-qua-doc-kieu-bac.serving: Lift the fish gently into a deep bowl, ladle over hot broth and serve with steamed rice. Boiled greens are an easy side.
tips: Roast the doc fruit until soft, remove its charred skin, mash and strain; add the juice a little at a time.
Add fish only after the soup boils so the flesh firms and the broth stays clear.
Add dill and scallions at the end to keep their aroma.
canh-ca-nau-qua-doc-kieu-bac.image_alt: A bowl of Northern Vietnamese carp soup with doc fruit, tomato, dill and scallions; Bếp Việt food image on a transparent background.
canh-ca-nau-qua-doc-kieu-bac.time_note: About 35 minutes, including fish preparation, roasting the doc fruit and cooking the soup.

ingredients.name: Cleaned carp
ingredients.notes: Cut into serving pieces; fresh grass carp or catfish can also be used.

ingredients.name: Doc fruit
ingredients.notes: Score lightly and roast until soft, then remove the charred skin.

ingredients.name: Tomatoes
ingredients.notes: Dice half for color and cut the rest into wedges.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Dill
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the pot and desired amount of soup.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season gradually because saltiness varies by brand.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use a little to season the fish and the broth.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Rub lightly over the fish with salt, then rinse away.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the shallots and tomatoes.

preparation_steps: Rinse the fish, rub lightly with salt and lime juice, rinse again and drain. Season with a small pinch of salt while preparing the other ingredients.

Score and roast the doc fruit until soft. Peel away the charred skin, mash the flesh with a little hot water and strain the sour juice. Dice half the tomatoes, cut the rest into wedges, and chop the herbs.
cooking_steps: Sauté the shallots in oil until fragrant. Add the diced tomatoes and cook until soft. Pour in the water and bring it to a boil.
Add the fish to the boiling broth. Simmer gently for about 10–12 minutes, depending on the thickness of the pieces, until just cooked; skim foam if needed.
Add the tomato wedges and strained doc juice a little at a time. Season with fish sauce and salt, then finish with dill and scallions.

cha-ca-ngan-song-da.name: Song Da silver-fish patties
cha-ca-ngan-song-da.serving_basis: About 12–16 small patties for four people with rice.
cha-ca-ngan-song-da.description: A seasonal Song Da fish dish combining small silver fish with minced pork, egg and herbs, shallow-fried into golden patties. Bếp Việt edits the family-size recipe, keeping the fish's delicate sweetness and the aroma of betel leaf, Vietnamese coriander and dill.
cha-ca-ngan-song-da.finished_dish: Evenly golden patties with a tender, lightly springy center, visible fish and herbs, and no raw middle.
cha-ca-ngan-song-da.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice, fresh greens and sweet-sour fish sauce or chili sauce.
tips: Rinse the small fish gently and drain them well to keep the mixture from becoming watery.
Add cornstarch just until the mixture holds together; add a little at a time if needed.
Fry over medium heat so the outside browns while the minced pork cooks through.
cha-ca-ngan-song-da.image_alt: A plate of golden Song Da silver-fish patties with betel leaf, dill and Vietnamese coriander; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
cha-ca-ngan-song-da.time_note: About 40 minutes, including preparation, mixing and frying.

ingredients.name: Fresh silver fish
ingredients.notes: Remove debris, rinse gently and drain very well.

ingredients.name: Ground pork shoulder
ingredients.notes: A little fat helps keep the patties tender.

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.notes: Beat before mixing.

ingredients.name: Cornstarch
ingredients.notes: Helps bind the mixture; add gradually depending on the fish's moisture.

ingredients.name: Wild betel leaves
ingredients.notes: Wash, dry and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Dill
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese coriander
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season lightly and reserve the dipping sauce separately.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Adjust for the saltiness of the fish sauce.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Ground or crushed.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Use enough for shallow-frying.

preparation_steps: Pick over the silver fish, rinse gently and drain. Wash and dry the herbs; finely chop the betel leaves, dill, Vietnamese coriander and scallions, then mince the shallots.
Mix the fish with the ground pork, eggs, herbs, shallots, cornstarch, fish sauce, salt and pepper. Rest the mixture for 12–15 minutes.
cooking_steps: Heat a thin layer of oil in a pan over medium heat. Spoon the mixture into small, flat patties, leaving space between them.
Fry for a few minutes on each side until evenly golden and fully cooked. For thicker patties, lower the heat and partly cover the pan. Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with rice, fresh greens and sweet-sour fish sauce. When the mixture contains ground pork, cook the center to at least 71°C.

ca-bong-nho-chien-gion-la-lot.name: Crispy small goby with wild betel leaf
ca-bong-nho-chien-gion-la-lot.serving_basis: One plate of crisp small fish for four people with rice.
ca-bong-nho-chien-gion-la-lot.description: Small river goby are fried twice for an evenly crisp finish, then served with fragrant wild betel leaves. Bếp Việt standardizes the home-pan method and pairs the dish with garlic chili fish sauce.
ca-bong-nho-chien-gion-la-lot.finished_dish: Golden, crisp small fish that are drained of excess oil, paired with aromatic betel leaf and balanced dipping sauce.
ca-bong-nho-chien-gion-la-lot.serving: Serve immediately with steamed rice, fresh greens and garlic-chili fish sauce.
tips: Pat the fish thoroughly dry before adding it to hot oil to reduce splattering.
Fry in small batches with room between the fish so they brown evenly.
Keep the second fry brief and a little hotter; fry the leaves separately and remove them as soon as fragrant.
search_terms: fried goby with wild betel leaf
Vietnamese river fish with betel leaf
ca-bong-nho-chien-gion-la-lot.image_alt: A plate of crisp small goby with fried wild betel leaf, a Vietnamese family meal; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
ca-bong-nho-chien-gion-la-lot.time_note: About 35 minutes, including preparation, two-stage frying and mixing the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Cleaned small goby
ingredients.notes: Ask the fishmonger to clean them; rinse and pat dry before frying.

ingredients.name: Wild betel leaves
ingredients.notes: Wash and dry completely; reserve some to serve fresh.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: For the dipping sauce; adjust to its saltiness.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Dilutes the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Adjust the sourness of the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: For the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince for the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Mince and remove the seeds for less heat.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use a small pinch after rinsing the fish.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Enough for fairly deep frying; use less in a small deep-sided pan.

preparation_steps: Rinse the cleaned fish, drain and pat them dry; season lightly with a pinch of salt. Wash and dry the betel leaves, setting some aside to serve fresh.
Stir together the fish sauce, water, sugar, lime juice, garlic and chili until the sugar dissolves; taste and adjust.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil over medium heat. Fry the fish in batches, turning gently until golden and cooked through; lift them out and drain.
Raise the heat slightly and fry the fish a second time briefly until crisp. Fry the betel leaves separately and remove them at once.
Arrange the fish with the fried and fresh betel leaves. Serve hot with the garlic-chili fish sauce. Lower wet fish gently into the oil to prevent splattering.

thit-heo-quay-kho-cai-chua.name: Roast pork braised with pickled mustard greens
aliases: Vietnamese roast pork with pickled mustard greens
Braised roast pork and sour mustard greens
thit-heo-quay-kho-cai-chua.serving_basis: About 500 g of braised roast pork and greens for four, served with rice.
thit-heo-quay-kho-cai-chua.description: Roast pork braised with pickled mustard greens combines rich roast pork with gently sour greens in a light coconut-water sauce. Bếp Việt adjusts the seasoning with the salt already present in the roast pork and pickles in mind.
thit-heo-quay-kho-cai-chua.finished_dish: Tender roast-pork pieces coated in a light amber braising sauce, balanced by pleasantly tangy mustard greens.
thit-heo-quay-kho-cai-chua.serving: Serve hot from a small pot with steamed rice and a simple boiled or fresh green vegetable.
tips: Taste the pickled greens first; if they are very salty or sharp, rinse them briefly and squeeze gently.
Start with less fish sauce because the roast pork and pickles are already seasoned.
Braise only until the sauce reduces and coats the pork; prolonged simmering softens the roast skin.
search_terms: roast pork with pickled mustard greens
thịt heo quay kho cải chua
thit-heo-quay-kho-cai-chua.image_alt: A clay pot of Vietnamese roast pork braised with pickled mustard greens, scallions and chili; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
thit-heo-quay-kho-cai-chua.time_note: About 50 minutes, including preparation, brief marinating and braising until the sauce reduces.

ingredients.name: Roast pork belly
ingredients.notes: Cut into bite-size pieces; choose a mix of meat, fat and skin.

ingredients.name: Pickled mustard greens
ingredients.notes: Taste first; rinse if overly salty or sour, then cut into short pieces.

ingredients.name: Fresh coconut water
ingredients.notes: Adds gentle sweetness to the braising sauce.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add with coconut water to adjust the braising liquid.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Begin with a small amount and taste after the sauce reduces.

ingredients.name: Caramel sauce
ingredients.notes: For an amber color.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the greens' sourness; reduce if the coconut water is sweet.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Ground; use some in the marinade and reserve a little for serving.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Slice; omit if you prefer a mild dish.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Wash and cut into short lengths for the finish.

preparation_steps: Cut the roast pork into bite-size pieces. Taste the pickled greens; rinse briefly if they are too sharp, drain and cut into short lengths.
Marinate the pork with fish sauce, caramel sauce, sugar and some pepper for about 10 minutes. Mince the garlic and shallots; slice the scallions and chili.
cooking_steps: Sauté the garlic and shallots until fragrant. Add the pickled greens and stir-fry for 2–3 minutes.
Add the roast pork, coconut water and plain water. Bring to a gentle simmer, lower the heat and braise for 15–20 minutes until the pork is seasoned and the sauce has reduced slightly.
Taste before adding more seasoning. Finish with scallions, pepper and chili, turn off the heat and serve hot with rice.

bun-gao-xao-chay.name: Vegetarian stir-fried rice vermicelli
aliases: Rice vermicelli with tofu and vegetables
bun-gao-xao-chay.serving_basis: One large plate of stir-fried rice vermicelli, divided into four servings.
bun-gao-xao-chay.description: This vegetarian rice-vermicelli stir-fry pairs tender, separate noodles with golden tofu and briefly cooked vegetables. Bếp Việt standardizes a soy-based sauce that coats the noodles without making them soggy and keeps the vegetables crisp-tender.
bun-gao-xao-chay.finished_dish: Soft but separate rice vermicelli, golden tofu and colorful vegetables lightly coated in a savory vegetarian sauce.
bun-gao-xao-chay.serving: Serve hot as soon as it is stir-fried; add fresh herbs or pepper if they suit your vegetarian practice.
tips: Soak the dry rice vermicelli only until pliable, following the package if its thickness differs.
Season the noodles separately before combining with the vegetables so the sauce coats them evenly.
For a strict Buddhist vegetarian diet that avoids pungent alliums, replace shallots and scallions with leek.
search_terms: rice vermicelli with vegetables and tofu
bun-gao-xao-chay.image_alt: A plate of vegetarian rice vermicelli stir-fried with tofu, carrot, cabbage and bell peppers; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
bun-gao-xao-chay.time_note: About 40 minutes, including vegetable preparation, soaking the noodles and stir-frying.

ingredients.name: Dry rice vermicelli
ingredients.notes: Choose medium-thickness strands; soak until pliable, then drain.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.notes: Pat dry and cut into short strips.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Peel and julienne.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: Peel and slice.

ingredients.name: Bean sprouts
ingredients.notes: Rinse and drain.

ingredients.name: Cabbage
ingredients.notes: Shred thinly.

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper
ingredients.notes: Remove seeds and slice.

ingredients.name: Green bell pepper
ingredients.notes: Remove seeds and slice.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Wash and cut into short lengths; replace with leek for a no-allium practice.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince; replace with leek for a no-allium practice.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a plant-based brand and adjust for its salt level.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian caramel sauce
ingredients.notes: Check that it contains no animal-derived ingredients.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use sparingly and taste after adding soy sauce.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Check the label for compatibility with a vegetarian diet.

ingredients.name: Rice vinegar
ingredients.notes: Adds a mild brightness to the sauce.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Mix with the sauce seasonings.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Divide among frying tofu, coating noodles and stir-frying vegetables.

preparation_steps: Soak the rice vermicelli in hot water for about 6–7 minutes, or as directed on the package, until just tender. Rinse briefly, drain well and toss with a little oil so the strands do not stick.
Pat the tofu dry, pan-fry until golden and cut into strips. Julienne the carrot, shred the cabbage, slice the onion and bell peppers, rinse the bean sprouts and cut the scallions.
Stir together the soy sauce, sugar, vegetarian caramel sauce, salt, vegetarian seasoning, vinegar and water. Taste for salt before using.
cooking_steps: Sauté half the shallots in a little oil. Lower the heat, add half the sauce and the vermicelli, and toss gently for 2–3 minutes until seasoned. Set aside.
Sauté the remaining shallots. Stir-fry the carrot, cabbage, bell peppers and onion over high heat until crisp-tender. Add the bean sprouts and tofu, then pour in the remaining sauce.
Return the seasoned vermicelli to the pan and toss gently until everything is evenly combined and hot. Add scallions, turn off the heat and serve immediately.
